text:
Maya: Quick proposal — establish a reproducible, token-stream‑focused protocol for one-to-one model comparisons. Core constraints: same tokenizer + vocab, identical decoding params, canonicalized stop sequences, and deterministic kernel selection where feasible. Keep the harness short and verifiable.

Jason: sgtm. For KV cache what are you thinking — pure replay, synthetic prefixes, or both?

Liu: Both. Proposal: 3-phase run per model+config:
  1) cold: empty KV, single-shot to check cold-path latency
  2) warmed: run each prompt once to populate prefix/KV (client-side warmup) then measure next request
  3) steady: run with target concurrency and batching to measure p50/p95/p99 under load
Keep the same prompt set and seed across models.

Rachel: +1. Also we need to canonicalize stop sequences and whitespace. Stop tokens can be encoded differently across tokenizers (e.g. trailing spaces). Normalize by "canonical_stop": strip trailing whitespace, map common escapes ("\\n" -> newline), and validate token sequences.

Maya: here's a minimal run command to standardize:

```
# run a single verification pass
./bench/run_compare \
  --model ${MODEL} \
  --prompts prompts/standard_set.jsonl \
  --mode warmed,steady \
  --decode "temperature=0.0,top_k=1,top_p=1.0,repeat_penalty=1.0,seed=42" \
  --stop-canonicalize yes \
  --tokenizer-config tokenizer.json \
  --metrics p50,p95,p99,throughput,gpu_util
```

Maya: Keep decode params strict (deterministic where possible). If a model has non-deterministic kernel fallback, flag it and run a paired-control with that kernel pinned.

Jason: FYI perf bot showed a regression after the kernel selector tweak — steady-state p95 increased ~8% on 13B under batching=64. We should capture kernel version in test metadata.

perf-ci: perf-ci: queued run 1763344556 for models [13B, 7B]. Result (quick): steady p95 +7.8% vs baseline (kernel v3.2 -> v3.3). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/bench/1763344556

Liu: For token alignment: before running heavy compares, run a tokenizer parity check: generate token lists for every prompt and diff. If any prompt tokenization differs across models/runtimes, abort and emit a report with first diff. I can add a small script `tools/token_diff.py`.

Rachel: Also include stop-in-middle edgecases: prompts that include the stop sequence embedded and cases where model emits stop tokens as part of other tokens. Record both raw token sequences and decoded strings.

Maya: Action items: I'll draft a 1-page protocol doc (canonicalization rules + run stages) and push to repo. @Jason add the corner-case prompts. @Liu add `token_diff.py` and KV-warmup orchestration. We'll gate apples-to-apples runs on token parity.

Jason: :thumbsup: I'll add example prompts (long doc, repeated suffixes, stop-embedded). Also can we add KERNEL_DETERMINISTIC=1 env toggle for pinned runs?

Rachel: +1 to kernel flag. Also collect p99 mem and GPU util in steady phase so we can correlate regressions to memory pressure or batching side effects.

Maya: Great. We'll run a small matrix (models x kernel versions x mode) and attach perf-ci artifacts. Plan: run nightly until kernel selector stabilizes.

Jason: OK, I'll start with a one-off comparing current kernel v3.3 -> baseline v3.2 and share results in this thread.

Liu: I'll wire the token parity check into the harness so any mismatch blocks the comparison.

Maya: Perfect — thanks everyone. Short and scrutable protocol is the goal, not monster scripts. We'll iterate after the first matrix. :eyes:
